s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain with radiation to the back, associated with anorexia and malaise, and a cystic mass in the pancreas
salient_findings: Vague, colicky epigastric pain radiating to the interscapular region
Cystic lesion in the head of the pancreas on abdominal ultrasound
Elevated platelet count and blood urea
key_facts: Pain relieved by changes in sitting position
No history of alcohol use, abdominal trauma, or pancreatitis
Abdominal ultrasound showed a cystic lesion in the pancreatic head
Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed an 11.8 cm cystic mass in the pancreatic head
Mild epigastric tenderness on deep palpation

shortlist.label: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass in the pancreatic head with no invasion of adjacent organs or lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystic neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic lesion in the pancreatic head with elevated blood urea and thrombocytosis

shortlist.label: Serous cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed, cystic mass in the pancreatic head with normal serum CA 19-9 level

shortlist.label: Pancreatic pseudocyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass in the pancreatic head with history of epigastric pain relieved by changes in sitting position

shortlist.label: Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass in the pancreatic head with mild epigastric tenderness on deep palpation and no signs of portal hypertension

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a large, well-circumscribed cystic mass in the pancreatic head without invasion of adjacent organs or lymphadenopathy, and the absence of a history of pancreatitis, is more consistent with a mucinous cystic neoplasm. The normal serum CA 19-9 level also supports this diagnosis, as elevated levels are more commonly associated with other conditions such as intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms or pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm
rejected.why: Typically presents with elevated serum CA 19-9 levels and is often associated with a history of pancreatitis

rejected.label: Serous cystadenoma
rejected.why: Usually presents as a smaller, multifocal lesion and is more common in the pancreatic body or tail

rejected.label: Pancreatic pseudocyst
rejected.why: Typically occurs in the setting of a history of pancreatitis, which is absent in this patient

rejected.label: Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm
rejected.why: Typically presents as a solid mass rather than a large cystic lesion
